Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

arm verb

equip with weapons

also armed, be armed, under arms, take up arms, lay down arms, by force of arms, armaments, arms race, arms (weapons)

classical

Cic. Caecin. 33: multitūdinem hominum coēgerit, armārit, īnstrūxerit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 273

armō, armāre, armāvī, armātum

verb, first conjugation

to arm, equip with weapons

Other words

  • armātus, armāta, armātum — armed

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 273

  • in armīs esse — be under arms, be armed

    also used · classical · Liv. 42.5.8: cum Thessalōs in armīs esse nūntiātum est (Lewis & Short s.v. cum); Traupman 273

  • arma capere — take up arms

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 11.1: contrā patriam scelerāta arma capere (Lewis & Short s.v. scelerō); Traupman 273

  • ab armīs discēdere — lay down arms

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 5.41.8 (Lewis & Short s.v. discēdō: “to lay down one’s arms”); Traupman 273

  • vī et armīs — by force of arms

    also used · classical · Liv. 1.19.1: urbem novam, conditam vī et armīs (Lewis & Short s.v. is); Cic. Sest. 79: cum omnia vī et armīs ēgerīs (Lewis & Short s.v. atquī); Traupman 273

  • apparātus bellī — armaments, the equipment of war

    also used · classical · Liv. 26.43: omnis apparātus bellī est (Lewis & Short s.v. armāmenta); Traupman 273

  • armōrum certāmen — an arms race

    also used · modern · Traupman 273

See also weapon, army.

SourcesLewis & Short: armo · Lewis & Short: arma

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
